Claim 1 (Currently amended): A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising [[one or more logic circuits configured to at least:]] __a hardware entropy source configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;__
__a function processor configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;__
__a pseudorandom number generator configured to be seeded with the second entropy value and to generate a random number using the second entropy value as a seed; and__
__a cryptographic processor configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number,__
[[receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source;apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; andproduce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number. produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.]] __wherein the function is a cryptographic hash function that combines the plurality of independent first entropy values with a secret key to generate the second entropy value.__

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the [[one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce]] __cryptographic processor is configured to produce__ the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

Claim 3 (Currently amended): The system[[of]] __of__ claim 1, wherein the [[one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least:]] __cryptographic processor is configured to:__
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 4 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the [[hardware source]] __hardware entropy source__ is a ring oscillator[[, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator]].

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the [[hardware source]] __hardware entropy source__ is a single hardware source[[, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source]].

Claim 6 (Cancelled)

Claim 7 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a [[permutation]] __cryptographic hash__ function[[, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function]].

Claim 8 (Currently amended): The system of claim 7, wherein the [[one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to:]] __function processor is configured to:__
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the [[permutation]] __cryptographic hash__ function to generate [[permuted]] __hashed__ groups of entropy values; and concatenate the [[permuted]] __hashed__ groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 9 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a [[hash]] __cryptographic hash__ function[[, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function]].

Claim 10 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a [[bit-mixer]] __cryptographic hash function that operates as a bit-mixer__[[, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer]].

Claim 11 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the [[one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to]] __function processor is configured to__ selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 12 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the [[one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to]] __function processor is configured to__ apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 13 (Currently amended): A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
[[receiving]] __generating__ a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a [[function]] __cryptographic hash function that combines the plurality of independent first entropy values with a secret key__ to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

Claim 14 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

Claim 15 (Previously presented): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator[[, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator]].

Claim 17 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source[[, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source]].

Claim 20 (Currently amended): The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the [[permutation]] __cryptographic hash__ function to generate [[permuted]] __hashed__ groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the [[permuted]] __hashed__ groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 21 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ is a hash function[[, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function]].

Claim 22 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ is a [[bit-mixer]] __function that operates as a bit-mixer__[[, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer]].

Claim 23 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 24 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the [[function]] __cryptographic hash function__ to generate the second entropy value.
